comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
For anyone that doesn't know anything about 3D modelling, if you want to show off AI generated models you really need to show things like a wireframe so you can see the topology and an untextured clay render style view.

Whenever you're showing fully textured models from a distance or in bad lighting it can completely hide bad models.

If we can't see what the underlining model is like then it's of little use.

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
That’s a fair point, and I completely agree. 👍

In fact, that’s one of the reasons I built the **review pipeline** into img2threejs. The goal isn’t just to make something that looks good from one camera angle, but to generate clean, editable geometry.

I’ll definitely add more wireframe, clay, and exploded-view showcases in the future so people can better evaluate the underlying topology instead of just the final render. Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
It wasn't specific to you really. Yours was actually a slightly better view than people normally show. Usually it's a distant view of a full textured model. Almost all current 3D gen models look good like that, however it's not until you get close up and start inspecting the textures and mesh that you realise it actually looks like crap and needs a tone of clean up work.

Normally when a 3D artist wants to show off the quality of their model they will show a wireframe so you can see the topology and then a clay render which is just a non textured view usually with AO so that you can see the surface of the model. This would highlight any surface problems with mesh.

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
Absolutely. That’s actually the standard I want img2threejs to be judged by.

The end goal isn’t a nice screenshot, it’s clean, procedural geometry that people can edit and build on. Showing only textured renders can definitely hide topology issues.

I’ll start including wireframe, clay renders, and close-up inspections in future showcases, and probably even publish the generated source alongside them so people can evaluate the actual geometry instead of just the visuals.

Really appreciate you bringing this up. Constructive feedback like this helps raise the bar for AI-generated 3D.

comments.author: ZealousidealShoe7998
comments.body: this is awesome but im wondering can this also be used for cad models ?

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
Thanks! 🙌 It depends on what you mean by CAD.

If you’re talking about **precise engineering or manufacturing CAD models**, then not yet. img2threejs is designed for procedural Three.js geometry, not dimensionally accurate CAD.

If you mean creating concept models for visualization, prototyping, or interactive web viewers, then yes, it can be a great starting point.

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
Haha 😄 Not quite! img2threejs generates **editable Three.js code**, not manufacturing-ready models.

If someone wants to 3D print it, they’d still need to convert it into a printable mesh and prepare it for fabrication. My focus is on games, XR, and interactive 3D experiences.
